📚 Today you learned

How to Read an FDA Briefing Document (Pre-AdCom Intelligence)

FDA posts briefing documents ≥2 days before AdCom — this is the agency's own analysis written by reviewers who will vote. Read order: (1) Clinical Review — FDA assessment of efficacy/safety. For CAPR: how do they treat 2.4% LVEF — "clinically meaningful" or "modest"? (2) Statistical Review — did FDA reproduce Capricor's p-values? (3) Executive Summary — FDA's stance. "Substantial evidence of effectiveness" = bullish. "Inadequate to demonstrate" = bearish.
Also: Complete Response Letter (CRL) — what FDA issues instead of approval when deficiencies found. CAPR received one in Jul 2025 (HOPE-2). This means the FDA review will be unusually scrutinizing HOPE-3 for the same concerns.

Rule: When investing in biotech pre-AdCom, always know if the pivotal trial used surrogate or clinical endpoints. Surrogate = faster approval path, higher panel rejection risk.
